subject: math

objective.text: Put equal parts together to make a shape. Name the parts halves, thirds or fourths.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Interpret equal shares in composite shapes as halves, thirds, and fourths.

explanations.title: Halves
explanations.text: 2 equal parts make a whole. Each part is called a half. Two halves make a whole.

explanations.title: Equal means the same size
explanations.text: To be halves, the 2 parts must be equal in size. They take up the same amount of space.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1: small triangle and parallelogram

explanations.title: Thirds
explanations.text: 3 equal triangles cover the trapezoid. 3 equal parts are called thirds.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2: trapezoid covered by triangles

explanations.title: Fourths
explanations.text: 4 equal small squares make 1 large square. 4 equal parts are called fourths.

examples.title: Halves of a hexagon
examples.text: 1 trapezoid covers half the hexagon. Put another trapezoid on. 2 equal trapezoids make the whole hexagon.

questions.text: Students pick up 13 parallelograms, 24 large triangles, 24 small triangles and 13 medium triangles. The rest are squares. There are 97 pieces in all. How many squares?
Join the smallest triangles into one larger triangle. How many parts does it have?
Are the 2 parts of this triangle equal?
What do we call 2 equal parts of a whole?

misconceptions.label: Calling unequal parts halves or thirds
misconceptions.description: Child counts the parts but does not check that they are equal in size.
detection_signals: Says 'halves' for 2 parts of different size or shape.
Says 'thirds' for a shape with only 2 parts, or with 3 unequal parts.
misconceptions.response_text: Halves must be 2 equal parts. Check the size of each part, not just how many.

assets_required.why_this_method: Blocks must have exact sizes so 2 trapezoids exactly cover a hexagon, 3 triangles a trapezoid, and so on.
assets_required.description: On-screen pattern blocks: hexagon, trapezoid, wide rhombus, triangle, square. The child drags blocks on top of a bigger shape to cover it.
must_show_exactly: All block sides the same unit length (trapezoid long side = 2 units)
assets_required.interaction: Drag, flip, slide and turn blocks; blocks snap to the outline.
assets_required.alt_text: Pattern blocks covering a bigger shape.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat pattern block shapes in plain colours (hexagon, trapezoid, rhombus, triangle, square), white background. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Two identical triangles must join exactly into 3 different shapes.
assets_required.description: The 2 smallest tangram triangles. They join to make a larger triangle, a square, or a parallelogram with no square corners. A small triangle with the parallelogram piece shows unequal parts.
must_show_exactly: Joined shapes: larger triangle, square, parallelogram
Unequal case: 1 small triangle + 1 parallelogram piece
assets_required.alt_text: Two small triangles joined into one shape.
assets_required.generation_caption: Two identical flat triangles in one colour on a white background. [Build by code]
